questions.question: Does `groups-invite-lifecycle-announcements.spec.ts` drive every scenario (invite, accept, decline, non-admin affordance-absence, admin moderation-Delete) through real browser contexts publishing via the app's own UI, with no `WebSocket.send`-to-relay shortcuts standing in for any step, and no scenario silently skipped or reduced to a stub `expect(true).toBe(true)` under time pressure? Are the announcement-visibility assertions genuine text/DOM checks (not merely 'element count increased by one', which would pass even if the wrong announcement type rendered)?

Is the new spec file named `groups-invite-lifecycle-announcements.spec.ts` (per stories.json's explicit note distinguishing it from the pre-existing, unrelated `groups-direct-invite-lifecycle.spec.ts` for epic-invite-rescind-and-member-removal), and does its filename correctly place it in the relay/Docker bucket (matching the `groups-*` glob) rather than accidentally landing in the no-relay fast bucket where a relay-dependent spec can never pass (per this project's documented e2e-bucket-naming trap)?

Could `e2e`'s `groups-invite-lifecycle-announcements.spec.ts` be deleted and rewritten using only the app's own public UI surfaces and the already-landed S2/S3/S5/S6/S7 behavior, without needing to import or reach into any module's internals (e.g. no direct import of `parseStructured`, `profileHandler`, or `welcomeSubscription` internals to short-circuit a scenario)? If any such reach-in exists, is it justified as the documented narrow exception for events the app cannot itself produce, and called out in the spec header?

Does the spec use at least two real browser contexts (per this project's e2e convention: 'boot a second `browser.newContext()`, sign in as that peer, and call the app's publish helper') for every scenario requiring a second participant (invite, accept, decline), rather than a single context simulating both sides? Does it use `expect.poll`/retrying assertions for relay-propagated state rather than a fixed `waitForTimeout` or a `reload()`+`isVisible()` race (both documented flake traps in this project), and was the invitee context's profile seeded via the documented safe re-seed-after-clearAppState pattern to avoid the profile-seed/clearState race?

Does this story correctly scope itself as a conformance oracle re-confirming AC-PROD-1/3, AC-DECLINE-3/9/10, and AC-IMMUT-1/3 at the assembled-system/UI level — one representative interleaving per scenario — rather than attempting (or omitting coverage that properly belongs to) the combinatorial ordering/interleaving search already owned by S9? Does it correctly exclude receive-side forgery/UI-bypass cases (AC-IMMUT-4 through 7, AC-CROSS-2) per acceptance-criteria.md's Manual Validation section, rather than either duplicating S8's unit coverage pointlessly or silently dropping it?

Is the spec resilient to this project's chronic ~4 rotating ~30s VM-latency timeouts on the full gate (a known pre-existing flake floor, not a regression signal) — i.e. does it use reasonable timeouts/retries consistent with the rest of the `groups-*` suite rather than either a flaky tight timeout or a masking-overlong one? Is the pass criterion correctly stated as the full 60-test `make test-e2e-all` gate (per CLAUDE.md's e2e-gate section), not a filtered/subset run of only this new spec file?

Does driving a direct contact-invite through the app's real UI (two browser contexts) produce a visible `invited` announcement in the group chat, confirming AC-PROD-1 at the assembled-system level? Provide (a) the test steps from invite-submission through announcement-visibility assertion, (b) the exact selector/text assertion used (matching S4's stable `data-testid`, not a generic 'any new message appeared' check), and (c) confirmation this is driven through `InviteMemberModal`'s real submit flow, not a fixture that bypasses the modal.

Does B's real join (through the app's own Welcome-processing flow, a second browser context) produce a visible `accepted` announcement, confirming AC-PROD-3 at the assembled-system level? Provide (a) the test steps from B's join through announcement-visibility assertion in A's view, (b) confirmation the join is driven through the app's real Welcome-acceptance UI (not a hand-constructed profile rumor), and (c) the exact assertion distinguishing an `accepted` announcement from an `invited` one (both now exist in the same chat, so the test must assert on the correct one).

Does B declining through the app's real UI trigger the gift-wrapped decline send (confirming AC-DECLINE-3's send-side behavior is reachable and functioning end-to-end), observable indirectly via A subsequently seeing the `declined` announcement and B's removal? Provide (a) the test steps for B's decline action in the app UI, (b) confirmation the test does not attempt to inspect the gift-wrap's encrypted bytes directly (that is S5's unit-test territory) but instead asserts the OBSERVABLE downstream effect at A's client, and (c) the exact assertion used.

Does the full decline scenario, driven end-to-end through the app, result in B (a genuinely pending, not-yet-joined member) being accepted as the decline's valid subject — confirming AC-DECLINE-9's tree-gate is satisfied in the real assembled flow, not bypassed by test setup accidentally making B a full member before declining? Provide (a) confirmation the test's B is in the pending-member state (invited, not joined) at the moment of decline, and (b) the assertion that A's client actually processed the decline (via the observable `declined` post + removal), rather than the decline silently no-op'ing due to a test-setup mistake that would falsely still make the overall test 'pass' on an unrelated code path.

Does the decline scenario observably confirm A's DD-7 ordering effects at the UI level — specifically, that B is removed from the visible member list AND the `declined` announcement appears (both effects present, per DD-10 steps 1-2) — using a retrying assertion (`expect.poll`/`toBeVisible` with retry) rather than a single-shot check that could race the relay-propagated update? Provide (a) both assertions (member-list removal and announcement visibility) as independent checks, and (b) confirmation neither assertion is satisfied by a stale pre-decline DOM snapshot (e.g. via a `reload()`+`isVisible()` pattern flagged elsewhere in this project as racing hydration).

For a non-admin viewer, does the spec assert the absence of both Edit and Delete affordances on at least one of the newly-visible `invite_lifecycle` announcements (invited/accepted/declined), confirming AC-IMMUT-1 at the UI level? Provide (a) the selector/assertion used to confirm ABSENCE (not merely that the test didn't click a button — an explicit query proving the affordance element does not exist or is not interactable), and (b) confirmation the viewing context in this assertion is genuinely a non-admin group member, distinct from the inviter/admin context used elsewhere in the same spec.

For an admin viewer, does the spec assert the moderation Delete affordance IS present on an `invite_lifecycle` announcement while Edit is NOT present, confirming AC-IMMUT-3 at the UI level? Provide (a) the selector/assertion for Delete-present, (b) the selector/assertion for Edit-absent (both required — a test only checking Delete-present could pass even if Edit were erroneously also shown), and (c) confirmation this admin-viewer assertion runs in the SAME spec against the SAME announcement message used for the non-admin AC-IMMUT-1 assertion, so the admin/non-admin contrast is genuinely exercised rather than tested against different messages that could differ for unrelated reasons.

Implementation discovered that `resolveInviteLifecycleSubjectDisplay` falls back to a truncated npub for B's `invited` announcement even well after A's client has processed later events for B (the `accepted` announcement in the SAME chat correctly resolves to 'Bob') — i.e. the earlier `invited` row's subject display does not appear to retroactively re-resolve once A's profileMap gains B's nickname. Is this consistent with AC-RENDER-1's contract (resolve from CURRENT `profileMap` at render time, npub-fallback when unknown — no claim of retroactive backfill), and with the identical documented precedent in `groups-member-admitted-announcement.spec.ts` ('C's copy of B's display name may still be the truncated-npub fallback... since B's real signed profile has not necessarily round-tripped')? Or does this reveal a genuine gap — e.g. a rendered announcement never re-renders once profileMap updates, versus simply not yet having received B's profile at all by that point? Note: this is an OBSERVATION from the actual e2e run (test-results snapshot showed 'npub1pmwlnjwv...5qrn843v was invited' persisting to the end of the spec), not a constructed edge case — the examiner should confirm which of the two explanations holds before treating it as either a non-issue or a defect.

During implementation, re-running this exact spec file twice in a row against the SAME strfry relay instance without wiping it between runs (`docker compose up -d --wait` once, then two sequential single-spec `run-e2e.mjs` invocations) reproduced a spurious 90s timeout on AC-PROD-3 (B's accept never propagated to A) — root-caused to relay-state contamination: `computeTestKeypairs()`'s per-spec-FILE identity salting (auth-helpers.ts) deduplicates identities ACROSS different spec files but does nothing to protect a SAME file re-run against an unwiped relay, so the second run's B/C had duplicate stale Welcomes/invitations queued alongside the fresh ones. A relay wipe (`docker compose down -v` + `up -d --wait`) before the THIRD run made all 8 tests pass cleanly with no changes to the spec. Since `make test-e2e-all` (the actual gate) always wipes the relay exactly once before running the full 60-test suite exactly once, does this hazard ever manifest in the real gate, or is it purely an artifact of ad hoc iterative dev-loop re-runs against a stale container that the examiner should be careful not to mistake for spec flakiness?
